answer.rationale: memory_b1 (rollback cleared checkout error spike, prior build stable) and memory_b6 (staged release gating caught bad builds, canary surfaced regressions inside an hour) directly support rollback. Write path p99 is 5x target, confined to the primary region, with a release 2 hours ago — classic regression pattern. Rollback reverses the most likely cause without dropping writes (prior build stable, rollback finished without customer impact per b1). Settled at peak makes capacity/failover risky: failover shifts heavy settlement traffic mid-peak (b2 was benign but here writes are heavy and b3's headroom is already in use). Circuit breaker (b4) would drop writes — violates the primary objective. Read replicas (b5) don't address write-path latency. One intervention: rollback.
